title: Tamna
capsule: Tamna was the indigenous kingdom of Jeju Island (Cheju), off the southern coast of the Korean peninsula, with legendary foundation attributed to three progenitors — Go, Yang, and Bu — who emerged from the volcanic ground at the site now called Samseonghyeol in Jeju City. By the first century CE the island maintained trade contacts with Han China, Yayoi Japan, and the Samhan states of the peninsula, and became a tributary of Baekje by 498. After Silla absorbed Baekje (660) and then itself fragmented, Tamna briefly regained independence before being subjugated by Goryeo in 938 and formally annexed as a prefecture in 1105. A residual kingdom under the Go-clan Seongju lords continued under Goryeo and early Joseon sovereignty until 1404, when King Taejong of Joseon abolished the autonomous status entirely.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territory — Jeju Island — is unambiguous; the polity's political extent and the dating of its various tributary and autonomous phases rest on Korean dynastic annals and are accepted but difficult to verify archaeologically.
